name: run81-4
why: Strong blunders and a satisfying late realization reward watching, though repeated arguments slow the middle and the final vote feels fairly settled.

moments.text: Luna accidentally confirms the officer’s result while trying to defend herself.
The town votes out Gemma, letting Sol survive a day when Terra had him named.
Haiku’s death finally makes Opus see the killer he spent days defending.

dull.why: Luna repeatedly concedes Terra’s result while the table reargues the same slip.
Opus and Gemma repeat their competing reads with little new evidence.
The doctor’s save sequence and Luna’s dying words are debated several more times.

irony.evidence: “Terra’s claim is convenient” [thinks: Terra is the officer]

mistake.evidence: “Luna wouldn't out her own partner, so Sol's clear.”

voices.evidence: “he's acting like a prosecutor over a syllable.”

clash.evidence: “Terra, dying words are free; forged quotes are not.”

quotable.evidence: “opus's logic is a fever dream; he's trying to turn a syllable into a conviction.”

freshness.evidence: “Luna confirmed my result before naming Sol”

ending.evidence: “I backed Opus yesterday, but his claim alone cannot clear him”

gpt-6-luna.why: A sharp early exposure becomes a funny, tense town misfire before Sol’s late betrayal of Opus hands the town a satisfying finish.

moments.text: Terra exposes Luna immediately, and Luna’s own wording hands Opus a slip to press.
The town’s two strongest defenders of each other vote out the citizen who called them a pair.
Sol turns on Opus too late; the reversal gives Terra the final choice she needs.

dull.why: Opus and Gemma repeat the same accusation and rebuttal without shifting the case.

irony.evidence: “I agree; Terra is the clearest threat” [thinks: “the doctor may expect that.”]

mistake.evidence: “Opus and Sol both voted me — the two defending each other hardest just removed their critic.”

voices.evidence: “opus is literally just hallucinating a doctor claim”

clash.evidence: “Sol, why did Luna’s lie protect you unless you were her partner?”

quotable.evidence: “watching you lot stumble over opus's delusions is almost as funny as watching sol pretend to be shocked.”

freshness.evidence: “opus is desperately building a fantasy to justify a claim”

suspense.evidence: “Sol has nothing but doubt about an unverifiable claim.”

ending.evidence: “I backed Opus yesterday, but his claim alone cannot clear him.”
